title: Introduce Retrieval Authoring Studio browser extension and lightweight toolkit
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds a browser extension and companion examples for an in-browser Retrieval Authoring Studio: capture content, build RAG templates, preview structured responses, and opt-in telemetry. Includes docs, a Node helper, and CI smoke tests.
description: Motivation: shipping high-quality RAG features depends on authoring ergonomics and quick iteration loops. This PR introduces the "Retrieval Authoring Studio" (a light browser extension + example toolkit) to make it fast for engineers and content authors to capture snippets, construct retrieval + prompt templates, and validate structured outputs before committing configs to production. The extension is intentionally offline-first and privacy-conscious: embeddings can be produced via a local embedding shim, or proxied to Redwood with explicit key input. Key pieces: 1) browser extension that captures page fragments, normalizes text, attaches metadata (source URL, DOM selector), and stores packs locally; 2) a small Node-based example helper (examples/ra-studio/node-helper) that shows how to: create an index, run similarity search, and call Redwood's hosted or dedicated inference endpoints with a template; 3) authoring UI examples (examples/ra-studio/ui) that demonstrate structured-output validation hooks and streaming previews; 4) docs updates (docs/ra-studio) with step-by-step authoring walkthroughs and a troubleshooting section for common embedding/encoding mismatches; 5) a minimal telemetry shim (opt-in) that emits anonymized event summaries for feature usage and authoring regressions so teams can iterate on templates. Checklist: - [x] Extension captures fragments, stores packs, and exposes export/import JSON. - [x] Node helper implements index and simple async re-ranker example. - [x] UI examples include structured-output validation and test fixtures. - [x] Docs site pages added with screenshots and a quick smoke-run. - [x] CI smoke test that runs the node-helper against a local vector store emulator. Security/privacy notes: extension never ships keys; users must paste an API key for temporary testing or use the local embedding shim. Telemetry is opt-in only; events are coarse (counts, latencies, anonymized templates) and documented in docs/ra-studio/telemetry.md. Testing: unit tests added for text normalization, a small E2E smoke job runs the node helper with the emulator in CI. Rollout: merged to main; we will soft-launch examples on the examples portal and monitor opt-in telemetry (if any) for early adopter feedback. Related: ENG-2041 tracks adding richer template assertions, PM-78 is the product brief for authoring workflows.
